spans.content: 4. CONCLUSIONS
In this experiment, through theoretical calculations and
molecular dynamics simulations, the diference between
thiamine and the leveling agent JGB was compared, and it
was determined that the adsorption capacity and adsorption
behavior of thiamine on the copper surface would inhibit the
deposition of copper better. By conducting CV and CP tests
on leveling agent JGB and new leveling agent thiamine, the
study shows that the CV oxidation peak area obtained after
adding thiamine is smaller than that of adding JGB, and the
potential diference of thiamine at high and low rotational
speeds
\triangle \eta = 8 7 ~ \mathrm { m V } > 5 0 ~ \mathrm { m V } ,
suggesting its potential as a
leveling agent. Through EIS testing, it was found that the
addition of thiamine not only inhibited the
\mathrm { C u } ^ { 2 + } \to \mathrm { C u } ^ { + }
reaction but also suppressed the
\mathrm { C u } ^ { + } \to \mathrm { C u }
reaction. Through
electroplating experiments, it was found that thiamine has a
leveling efect on copper deposition and can be applied to
wafer microhole electroplating. Moreover, in wafer electro-
plating, it was found that without adding inhibitors, only 55
mg/L Cl<sup>−</sup>, 6 mg/L SPS, and 4 mg/L thiamine as leveling
agents can achieve a good filling efect.
